entries.description: Operator set pathAwareCritique: advisory.
Registered session 1; confirmed prerequisite 109 complete (S1/S2 VERIFIED, S3/S4 WAIVED); read the four-file preload; all three DABBLER_* keys present.
Routed step-3.5 analysis (analysis, excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0091); authored ai-assignment.md with routing plan, per-source budget note, and departures.

Re-ran the architecture panel on the 109-corrected registry: Opus 5 direct (operator ruling, $0), Sonnet 5 routed ($0.0367), GPT-5.6 Sol routed ($0.1056). All three GO; unanimous that the perf case is false and the density trade is the operators call.

Built scripts/perf-harness.ts; measured at 0/10/100/500 synthetic sets plus the real repo. Empty tree = ~102ms host work, 0.3ms of it scanning; the rest is a synchronous git worktree list subprocess in discoverRootsWithFamilies(). Fixed a double-counting attribution bug in the harness before recording any number.

Built and ran a throwaway extension in a real Extension Development Host (VS Code 1.131.0): contributes.submenus gives a hierarchical menu two levels deep; group:inline renders platform icons that do not overlap the label; getChildren is lazy per level and not called at all until the view is visible.

Rendered the worst-case row at default and wide panel widths. Found that TreeItem.description is dropped entirely when the label truncates, so the 3/5 fraction is invisible at working width for every real set name.

Eyeballed the operator status SVGs in both themes (operator-notes wrinkle 2). All four carry #ffffff/#000000 beyond the documented green/grey; not-started.svg is nearly invisible on a light theme and in-progress.svg loses its ring. 16mm authoring scales fine (wrinkle 3).

Put the density trade to the operator with rendered evidence. Decisions: drop the fraction from set rows entirely (progress read from session glyphs); keep four sessions and sequence S3 internally (tests green before deletion).
Wrote s1-migration-decision.md: panel verdict, measurements, four spike answers, the operator-confirmed mapping table, plan adjustments, and an explicit GO with the performance claim withdrawn.
Discovery round (fan-out 2, gpt-5-6-sol x2, anthropic excluded): ISSUES_FOUND, 4 blocking Majors, $0.8240. Supplementary completeness pass: VERIFIED, nothing new, $0.0541.

Accepted all 4 findings, none disputed. Withdrew the startup over-claim (S4 must now measure, not confirm); re-spiked inline actions at the real four-action count and REVERSED the result (label erased at min width) -> capped at 2; added a ranked icon precedence table, spike-proven at min width. Sidecar: s1-remediation-round-1.md.

Remediation-review on the fix delta: VERIFIED, 0 findings, 1 fix accepted + 2 accepted-with-modification, 0 rejected, $0.1495. Two nits: min-width check for two inline actions (already a recorded S4 residual) and a precedence-order mismatch between the spike comment and the binding table (fixed, per L-065-1). Operator pre-authorized 2 extra rounds and a third-provider round; NEITHER was needed.
Authored disposition.json (status completed, verdict VERIFIED, next_orchestrator recorded with the routed recommendation and its budget caveat); committed and pushed; ran close_session.

close_session gate FAILED: the Set-084 close backstop ran round 4 over the whole session diff and found 3 Majors - three of four startup buckets unmeasured, the withdrawn over-claim surviving in four echoes, and the required before/after never produced.

Accepted all 3. Built scripts/activation-harness.ts: activate() 338.8ms, resolveWebviewView() 0.1ms, renderer payload 110376 bytes -> 3 of 4 buckets now measured. Rewrote all four over-claim echoes (L-065-1, which this session had cited without applying). Captured the shipping renderer as the before image, which revealed the webview WRAPS set names where a TreeView truncates; operator confirmed the final mapping a second time, accepting truncation.

Round 5 remediation-review REJECTED the activation fix (1 Major). Disputed the part demanding a native-tree measurement that cannot exist until S2; spent the operator-preauthorized third-provider round on it. gemini-2.5-pro (neither anthropic nor openai) UPHELD the verifier and ruled against the orchestrator: the impossible half was answered while the possible half - real cold activation of the current extension - was left undone. Dispute withdrawn.

Built scripts/cold-activation.js: fresh Node process per rep, module load inside the measurement, real dist bundle. module load 54.3ms, activate() 336.5ms, cold total 389.9ms. activate() cold ~= warm (vindicating that figure) but module load was a real 54.3ms the warm harness excluded. Superseded the warm activateMs; corrected the doc guess that module loading explained the undecomposed time. Two attempts at renderer first paint abandoned rather than faked.

Round 6 rejected the cold-Node harness on the same ground (never launches VS Code). Bounded loop exhausted -> STOPPED to the operator per the constitution rather than opening another cycle. Operator authorized one bounded real-host attempt.

Real-EDH baseline attempted TWICE and failed both times (palette timeout; then no treeitem visible in 60s). Spec left SKIPPED with both failure modes and an S4 fix instruction, not deleted and not left red (L-064-12). Recorded honestly: all activation figures remain stub-measured; the verifier was right through three rounds.

Operator instruction: route the issue to a third party. Routed to gemini-3.1-pro-preview (Google; third party to the anthropic orchestrator and openai verifier, and a DIFFERENT model from the first adjudicator). Verdict MAY_CLOSE, endangers_s2_s4=false: the 102ms floor is the operative finding, the perf claim is withdrawn, S3 deletion is reversible and S4 is the release gate. It also judged the verifier and first adjudicator to have conflated literal spec compliance with the go/no-go requirement. Recorded its four mandatory disclosures in the decision doc.

Real-host baseline SUCCEEDED on the fifth attempt. Two distinct bugs were mine: launchVSCode was given tmpPath instead of handle.repo_root (so VS Code opened a workspace with no session sets), and the run depended on triggerRefresh, whose command palette flaked in 3 of 4 attempts. Dropping the forced refresh was also the more correct measurement. Results: launch->first row 11582ms, view open->first row 5102ms, medians of 3, tight variance. The stub harnesses had reported ~390ms cold bootstrap - understating the user-visible cost by more than 10x. The verifier refused those figures three times and was right on the merits, not on a technicality. Decision doc corrected throughout: performance is now a real but unquantified SECONDARY justification rather than withdrawn.

Round 8 raised 2 Majors, both accepted. F9: I attributed the 5.1s aggregate to webview cost (only ~124ms scan survives) without decomposing it - an over-claim in the opposite direction, withdrawn; the four-buckets-at-four-scales requirement is now named as still undelivered in the real host. F10: section 6 still carried pre-success text (spec skipped, no real-host number, measure INCLUDING the refresh) contradicting section 2 - L-065-1 for the third time in one session, caused by replacing headings without rewriting the bodies. S4 now has exactly one canonical measurement instruction.

Real-host aggregate measured at 10/100/500 sets: view-open to first row 5330/5215/5470 ms, reproduced independently at 5297/5328/5495 ms. FLAT across a 50x set-count change, which rules out the per-set scan (242ms at 500 sets) and per-row DOM construction as the cause. Fixed startup cost, deliberately unattributed. Also recorded a direct conflict between spec step 3 (per-bucket real-host timings) and the session plan (Touches: nothing shipping) - honoured the latter, assigned instrumentation to S2.

Operator adjudicated 2026-08-05: accept the delivered evidence (bucketed stub at four scales + real-host aggregate baseline). Closing WAIVED on operator attestation with the residual recorded, not VERIFIED.
Registered Session 2 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high); preload read; provider keys confirmed present.

Read spec Session 2 plan, operator-notes (2026-08-04 four-level tree + status icons + fraction; 2026-08-05 verification-loop discipline and the S4 sub-second startup gate), and s1-migration-decision.md in full.

Confirmed Session 1 complete (verdict WAIVED) and its go/no-go: GO. Surveyed SessionSetsModel, CustomSessionSetsView, ActionRegistry, types.ts, fileSystem.ts, package.json contributions, the S1 spike extension, and the Layer 2/3 harnesses.
Routed step-3.5 analysis (analysis, excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0164, truncation-clean); appended the Session 2 block to ai-assignment.md recording three departures from the analyst.

Carried the already-parsed sessions[] ledger onto SessionSet via normalizeLedgerSessions (tolerant, per-entry drop); optional field so Layer-2 fixtures need no update. Enables the fourth tree level with no additional disk read.

Extracted CustomSessionSetsView.buildModules into providers/moduleAssembly.assembleVisibleModules and refactored buildBucketPayloads onto a new shared orderedBuckets(), so both Explorer surfaces compute one module list and one bucket ordering.

Wrote providers/workExplorerTreeModel.ts (pure, no vscode): four-level node union, per-level children, row descriptors, the ranked icon-precedence table, and the semicolon-delimited contextValue vocabulary.

Wrote providers/WorkExplorerTreeProvider.ts (lazy getChildren, per-refresh scan memoisation, getParent for reveal, set-row activation command); registered via createTreeView ALONGSIDE the webview, which stays default and first.

Generated package.json contributions from ROW_ACTIONS: second view (collapsed), two submenus, 20 view/item/context entries, 2 inline module actions (S1 cap). Taught 3 existing module palette commands to accept an optional tree node rather than minting new command ids.

Added utils/startupTiming.ts (module load / activate / resolveWebviewView / first tree roots), emitted only when DABBLER_STARTUP_TIMING_PATH is set. First paint deliberately left to Layer 3 rather than instrumenting a webview S3 deletes.

Settled the status-icon theme question by RUNNING code: icon-render-mechanism.spec.ts measured a real Extension Development Host and found TreeItem.iconPath renders as background-image with mask-image:none, so currentColor cannot work - overturning both S1 and the step-3.5 analyst. Repointed to media/light + media/dark (operator authored both sets mid-session).

Added 5 Layer-2 suites (tree model, provider, menu parity, module assembly, ledger rows, startup timing, icon assets) and a Layer-3 native-tree spec. Updated two pre-existing source-scan/allowlist tests the refactor legitimately moved.

Build clean; typecheck clean; lint 7 errors/61 warnings ALL pre-existing (none in new or changed files). Layer 2: 1907 passing, 0 failing. Layer 3 FULL suite: 32 passed, 0 failed (16.9 min), including both new native-tree specs.
Phased discovery round 1 (fan-out 2, both gpt-5-6-sol, anthropic auto-excluded, $1.3364): VERDICT VERIFIED, ZERO blocking findings, 12 nits across the two calls with five raised convergently by both.

Fixed all 12 nits despite the round being non-blocking (two were real correctness defects: duplicate/non-positive session numbers colliding row identity, and webview resolve marks not first-wins). Recorded a 13th found by running the suite: real-host-baseline.spec.ts was overwriting S1 committed measurement of record - S1 artifact restored, re-run kept as S2 evidence, write gated behind DABBLER_WRITE_EVIDENCE=1 (same class as the icon-probe nit, fixed at every sibling site).

Discovery round 2 over the SHIPPED state (fan-out 2, both gpt-5-6-sol, $1.1802, cross-round ledger carried): VERDICT VERIFIED, 0 blocking. Round 1 remediation held - nothing reappeared. Raw artifacts carry 4 nits (CLI structured parse said 0); dispositioned in s2-remediation-round-2.md. Two doc claims corrected; two code nits assigned to S3 with the fix spelled out, because S3 owns that surface, the round is Minor-only, and touching code mid-close-run is the invalidation pattern the operator just banned.

Registered Session 3 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high); preload read (constitution, project-guidance, lessons-learned, CLAUDE.md); all three DABBLER_* keys present; no decision-review-queue entries.

Read the spec's Session 3 plan and config block (full tier, requiresUAT true -> S4, requiresE2E true -> L-064-12 at full strength HERE, pathAwareCritique advisory -> S4). Read operator-notes: the 2026-08-05 test-run policy names S3 as the non-negotiable full-Layer-3-at-close session, and the verification-loop discipline note binds the phased bounds.

Confirmed S1 complete (WAIVED, GO) and S2 complete (VERIFIED). Verified every S2 Create exists on disk (providers/WorkExplorerTreeProvider.ts, workExplorerTreeModel.ts, moduleAssembly.ts, commands/workExplorerTreeCommands.ts, utils/startupTiming.ts, media/light + media/dark glyph pairs). Surveyed the deletion surface: client.js 1201 lines, tree.css 723, CustomSessionSetsView.ts 977; 11 of 15 Layer 3 specs drive the webview through openSessionSetsView.

Routed step-3.5 analysis (analysis, excl. anthropic -> gpt-5.6-luna, $0.0170, truncation-clean). FIRST ATTEMPT LOST ITS PAID OUTPUT to an AttributeError on a metadata line after the call returned - L-079-1's exact warning, recorded rather than hidden; the script now writes result.content to disk before touching any other attribute.

Routed the one genuine design question — the stacked WebviewView's PRESENCE RULES (architecture, excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0146). Verdict: a `when`-gated view, with the host loading the webview's OWN systemStatusHtml.js in-process rather than reimplementing its fault rules (no parity test needed because there is one implementation). Departed from it on two points, both recorded: viewsWelcome is NOT contributed (it would only fire in the no-folder case the webview already covers more richly), and the manifest fault ships in ONE channel (TreeView.message) not two.

Re-expressed the Layer 3 behavioural specification against the native surface, routed as test-generation (excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0918, 29.8k in / 5.5k out). Promoted 8 native-tree helpers into electronLaunch.ts, located by the presence of a .monaco-list rather than by pane TITLE so no spec had to change in the commit that flipped the shipping surface. 15 Layer 3 specs -> 14: 5 deleted (session-sets-tree split, multi-in-progress folded, context-menu-quickpick superseded, migration-cta + migration-cta-v4 merged), 6 rewritten, 3 new. REJECTED two of the analyst's verdicts on the record: loading-state.spec.ts and the four Getting Started scenarios are NOT superseded — the form is untouched by this migration.

Discharged S2 residual 1: WorkExplorerTreeProvider now retains manifestFaults and reports them through an onDiagnostic sink that extension.ts binds to TreeView.message. Reports on EVERY recompute including the clean case, so a repaired manifest clears the message rather than leaving the workspace permanently accused. describeManifestFaults is pure and exported so Layer 2 can pin the wording without a TreeView.

package.json: the native tree is the shipping `Work Explorer` (no visibility, no when); the webview becomes `Setup & Status`, stacked above, gated on dabblerSessionSets.setupNeeded; all five view/title actions retargeted to the tree (an action gated on a conditional view disappears with it); the activity-bar mark swapped to the circled-checkmark icon-2. extension.ts wires the diagnostic sink and the new context key, which fails toward VISIBLE.

providers/systemStatus.ts extracted (buildSystemStatus + isSetupNeeded). CustomSessionSetsView.ts (977 lines) DELETED, replaced by SetupStatusView.ts (~270) carrying only the Getting Started form and the System Status strip; view id unchanged so saved layouts survive. Message protocol 8 -> 2 messages; the COMMAND_ALLOWLIST went with the dispatch channel it guarded (removing the surface beats allowlisting it).

client.js 1202 -> 400 lines; tree.css 724 -> 277 (incl. the 0.48.0 ellipsis rule and the action strip whose comment records the Set 108 swallowed-click defect); SnapshotPayload.modules removed. Deleted outright: suppressionState.ts, moduleActionNarrowing.ts, both poc-nine-modules scripts, the two dead QuickPick item builders, and three orphaned webview mockup/screenshot assets. Routed deletion/orphan review (code-review, excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0450) drove the scope; two of its coverage_at_risk claims are rejected on the record.

Repaired 8 Layer-2 suites that scanned the deleted view BY PATH. Live invariants RETARGETED (the never-write-the-manifest trust boundary now polices 5 passive paths instead of 2; the blocked-badge retirement follows the badge to the tree descriptors); dead contracts DELETED; two behaviours MIGRATED from source scans to real assertions on setDescriptor/setTooltip. The Set 110 S2 view-contribution test became the single shipping-surface contract. Layer 2: 1866 passing / 0 failing.

Wrote overlay-click-swallow.spec.ts — the operator's 'seed a regression and prove Layer 3 catches it' step, as a PERMANENT falsifier rather than a one-off manual demo. It seeds the Set 108 shape (flow-height overlay above tree content, pointer-events live) in the real workbench frame, requires a NORMAL non-forced click to fail, then removes it and requires the identical click to pass. If the seed fails to break the click the test fails loudly, because an unfalsifiable guard reads as coverage.
complete
entries.status: Targeted Layer 3 across every new and rewritten spec. First pass 18/22; four failures, ALL in the tests rather than the product, and all four are my own over-claims: (a) native-tree.spec.ts still opened the pane by its Session 2 preview TITLE via a local helper I had not replaced; (b) the same file's fixture stamped module slugs from its own retired manifest copy after I re-pointed it at the shared one; (c) cancellation-state-file asserted an empty `Cancelled` bucket renders with '0 sets' - orderedBuckets emits that fourth bucket ONLY when non-empty (the three defaults always render; Cancelled is conditional), so the webview's original toHaveCount(0) translated literally after all; (d) module-tier split module row text on a newline that is not there - VS Code renders label and description inline, so 'Greeter 3 sets' is one line. Each header comment now records the corrected reading, since (c) and (d) were both L-064-8: a claim about current behaviour written into a new doc and not checked.

entries.description: complete
entries.status: Self-review catch, no gate would have seen it: isSetupNeeded stats every PATH entry twice (the Python and Copilot-CLI presence probes) and evaluateContextKeys is called synchronously inside activate(). Filesystem stats, not subprocess spawns, so small - but this set exists because of startup cost and S4 has a sub-second view-open gate. Moved that one evaluation behind setImmediate so activate() does not pay it. Watcher-inventory allowlist line numbers updated twice as extension.ts shifted.

entries.description: complete
entries.status: Full Layer 3 suite (the operator's non-negotiable for a session touching the Explorer rendering surface). First full run: 30 passed / 3 failed, and all three were specs OUTSIDE the set I had rewritten - which is exactly the coverage a targeted run cannot buy. (a) real-host-baseline.spec.ts measured the WEBVIEW's cold launch-to-first-row through the deleted iframe; RETARGETED at the native tree through the identical protocol, writing s3-native-tree-baseline.json rather than overwriting S1's before-number, so S4 inherits a working after-harness. (b) icon-render-mechanism.spec.ts still located its pane by the Session 2 preview title. (c) vsix-first-run-walkthrough hit a hidden assumption in a helper I wrote: openWorkExplorerTree waits 30s for a first row, but at that point a real venv+pip install is still running; switched to workExplorerPane, which does not wait. Second full run is the run of record.

entries.description: complete
entries.status: Phased discovery round 1 (fan-out 2, both gpt-5-6-sol, anthropic auto-excluded, $2.0296): ISSUES_FOUND, 1 blocking Major, 0 minor. The finding is sharper than 'flaky test': the new environment-fault Layer 3 test did not deterministically CAUSE a fault. Its stated reason (the workspace-initialization probe fails) was factually impossible - workspaceInitialized is hasAnySets || structureBuilt and the fixture creates a set - and it passed only because the Electron launcher's env allowlist happens to strip DABBLER_* keys, so the PROVIDER-KEY fault fired instead. On a runner that passed those keys through, the mandatory full-suite gate would have failed on the environment rather than the product.

entries.description: complete
entries.status: Supplementary completeness-critic pass ($0.9877), run BEFORE any remediation as the loop requires: VERIFIED, zero findings. Nothing joined the merge.

entries.description: complete
entries.status: Fixed the Major by making the fixture CAUSE a fault it controls (dabblerSessionSets.pythonPath pointed at a nonexistent file, which short-circuits the Python probe deterministically) and asserting the exact fault code, so the test can no longer pass on a fault it did not cause. Declined the verifier's suggested fix (use an empty workspace) on the record: that returns true on the !hasAnySets branch and stops exercising the fault path at all. B-lite acceptance checks run against BOTH states with outputs pasted in s3-remediation-round-1.md. TWO MORE defects fixed in the same round, both found by the full run rather than a verifier and both in code this session wrote: openDabblerContainer clicked the activity-bar icon unconditionally (VS Code icons TOGGLE, so the second call closed the sidebar and cost the walkthrough a 5-minute timeout), and the first fix for it guessed at the workbench's .checked markers, read them backwards, and turned one failure into three - replaced by an explicit reveal flag. Plus a third race: the scaffold writes modules.yaml BEFORE the lifecycle sets, so the SET COUNT is the completion signal, not the module row.
